title: Navimower 0.4.4-beta39

## Safety and validation hardening

This prerelease adapts several edge cases identified while cross-reviewing Navimower with `navimow_pro` v0.6.0. The changes are intentionally narrow: prefer retained mower state over starting a new task, validate only against authoritative map data, and keep diagnostics useful without weakening privacy.

- **Paused-returning Start is now resume-safe.** State `0221` is treated as a resumable paused return in the Home Assistant mower entity. Pressing Start while the mower is paused on its way to the dock now sends the existing Resume command instead of falling through to a new `reset=true` mowing start.
- **GPS tracker refuses the vendor no-fix `0/0` pair.** The native `device_tracker` no longer publishes `0.0, 0.0` as a real position, avoiding false Home Assistant zone transitions in the Gulf of Guinea.
- **Polled GPS no longer forces recorder churn.** `device_tracker.force_update` is explicitly false so unchanged cloud coordinates do not create a new recorder row on every coordinator refresh.
- **Zone-ID validation trusts only the decoded map.** `navimower.mow` and enabled `set_schedule` calls reject unknown explicit zone IDs only when `map.zones` is available from decoded geometry. Partial fallback zone lists are never used as proof that a real zone does not exist.
- **Existing schedules can always be switched off.** Forward-time, overlap and zone-membership checks apply when enabling a day. Disabling a vendor-app schedule is not blocked just because an already-stored plan is stale, overlapping or references a zone no longer present in the current decoded map.
- **Firmware versions stay useful in sanitized diagnostics.** Standalone dotted values such as `1.12.3.40` are preserved when they are under an explicit version/firmware field, while real network addresses elsewhere remain redacted. The support-report redaction contract is bumped to version 4.

No Navimower Map Card change is required for this release. No intentional changes are made to mowing history, map geometry, gate logic, cloud authentication or protocol behavior outside the safety cases above.
